analysis.title: Duolingo Inc. (DUOL) Q3'26 Earnings Review: Strong Bookings Momentum Follows Recent Turnaround on Users
key_insights: GS reiterates Neutral on DUOL and raises the 12-month price target to $140 from $135. Price was $128.00, implying 9.4% upside. The rating has been Neutral since Aug 8, 2024.
Q3'26 DAUs rose 29% y/y, accelerating from +23% in Q2 for the second consecutive quarter. Strength was broad-based across geographies, and management expects similar user growth into Q4.
Q3'26 bookings grew 12% y/y, about 400bps faster than Q2. GS reads this as monetization starting to align with user growth, an early positive indicator for 2027.
Q3'26 bookings, revenue and adj. EBITDA beat GS and consensus estimates and guidance. Management raised FY26 guidance on all three metrics.
Declining AI inference costs and internal efficiencies supported gross margin. Q3 gross margin was 72.8% vs 71.0% for both GS and consensus.

Management is pushing AI features through the Super Family Plan at roughly the same price point as Max. Q4 guidance implies modest sequential gross margin pressure from product investment and the Max-to-Super transition.
Operating expenses are expected to keep growing faster than revenue, and adj. EBITDA is guided roughly flat y/y in Q4 on AI investment, experimentation and employee costs.
Paid subscriber growth continues to lag DAU growth, as conversion and monetization benefits take time to arrive.
Management framed monetization as a multi-year effort covering subscription expansion, in-app purchases and higher quality advertising.
GS expects investors to watch whether sustained user growth and monetization build operating momentum, which could support a return to a growth-oriented valuation framework.

GS estimate changes: Q4'26 revenue $322mm (from $315mm), 2026 revenue $1,222mm (from $1,207mm), 2027 revenue $1,387mm (from $1,366mm), 2027 adj. EBITDA $381mm (from $370mm), 2027 GAAP EPS $4.21 (from $3.95).
Price target scenarios: downside $70, base $140, upside $200. The target blends an EV/Sales approach and a modified DCF on EV/GAAP EBITDA.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral kept on risk/reward at current levels. PT raised to $140 from $135 on updated estimates and management commentary after a Q3 beat.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees DUOL as a leader in language learning with users, engagement and monetization well above direct competitors, but keeps Neutral on risk/reward.

earnings_insights: DUOL Q3'26 reported (4 Nov 2026 note): total bookings $316mm vs GS $307mm and consensus $308mm. Total revenue $309mm vs GS $302mm and consensus $303mm.
DUOL Q3'26 reported: adj. EBITDA $79mm vs GS $76mm and consensus $76mm. Adj. EBITDA margin 25.5% vs GS 25.2% and consensus 25.1%.
DUOL Q3'26 reported: DAUs 65mm vs GS 62mm and consensus 62mm. MAUs 153mm vs consensus 147mm. Paid subscribers 13mm vs consensus 13mm, 1% above GS and 1% below consensus.
DUOL Q3'26 reported: subscription bookings $278mm vs GS estimate $262mm. Other bookings $38mm vs GS estimate $45mm, 16% below.
DUOL Q4'26 GS estimates (new, from old): bookings $382mm (from $380mm), revenue $322mm (from $315mm), adj. EBITDA $84mm (from $83mm), GAAP EPS $0.64 (from $0.55).
DUOL 2027 GS estimates (new, from old): bookings $1.47bn (from $1.45bn), revenue $1.39bn (from $1.37bn), adj. EBITDA $381mm (from $370mm), GAAP EPS $4.21 (from $3.95).
risk_factors: Faster or slower than expected user acquisition, from organic acquisition levels and returns on external marketing spend.
Better or worse than expected payer conversion, depending on the pace and impact of product enhancements.
Competitive intensity in language learning and in other categories including music and math.
Q4 gross margin pressure and opex growing faster than revenue.

key_data_points.context: Accelerated from +23% in Q2, second consecutive quarter of acceleration. Reported with Q3'26 results.
key_data_points.anchor: strong DAU growth (+29% YoY) was a standout

tension_points.bull_case: DAUs grew 29% y/y, bookings growth accelerated about 400bps q/q and FY26 guidance was raised, which GS calls an early positive indicator for 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Subscriber growth lags DAU growth, Q4 adj. EBITDA is guided roughly flat y/y, and opex is expected to grow faster than revenue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sustained user growth and engagement failing to translate into operating momentum, or a slower-than-expected payer conversion.

theme_stances.key_argument: Strong user growth and bookings acceleration are offset by risk/reward at current levels.
theme_stances.evidence: We reiterate our Neutral rating based on risk/reward
